extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of logic, metaphysics, and philosophy of mind
extracted.subtask_description: Defines and analyzes the core logical/metaphysical categories (Feelings, Substances, Attributes) and gives criteria for what counts as qualities, relations, and quantities, with guidance on how these are grounded in sensations or states of consciousness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge of objects limited to sensations and their order
rubrics_metrics.description: All we know of objects is the sensations which they give us, and the order of the occurrence of those sensations; the real nature of things in themselves is (at least for present faculties) an impenetrable mystery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is treated as the fundamental methodological premise: we must confine our claims about external objects to what is revealed by sensations and their systematic occurrence. Appeals to 'things in themselves' (noumena) or intrinsic nature go beyond what can be known.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Body (substance) as unknown external cause
rubrics_metrics.description: A body is conceived as the unknown external cause or substratum to which we refer sensations; matter is the name given to this substratum in philosophical discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although commonly conceived, the existence of matter cannot be proved by extrinsic evidence; belief in it is characterized as intuitive. For logical purposes treat 'body' as the cause of sensations, not as an object knowable beyond those sensations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Mind (substance) as unknown recipient/percipient
rubrics_metrics.description: Mind is conceived as the unknown sentient subject which has feelings (sensations, thoughts, emotions, volitions); we know nothing of the mind beyond the series of its states of consciousness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Like body, mind's inmost nature is unknowable; for logical analysis treat mind as the subject of states of consciousness and describe its attributes by reference to those states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes divided into Quality, Quantity, and Relation
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes (what can be predicated of Things) are commonly distributed under three heads: Quality, Quantity, and Relation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text proceeds to analyze each head in turn; for logical purposes one should define attributes by the sensations or states of consciousness on which they are grounded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality grounded on sensations (foundation of quality = sensation)
rubrics_metrics.description: When we ascribe a quality (e.g., whiteness) to a substance we mean that the presence of that substance excites in us a particular sensation; the sensation is the 'foundation' of the quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the purposes of logic adopt language compatible with either metaphysical view, but treat the sensation as the essential and provable part of a quality: 'When that [sensation] is proved, the quality is proved.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid positing occult or redundant causes (anti‑metaphysical principle)
rubrics_metrics.description: We should not posit an additional 'power' or occult cause beyond the factual relation that an object excites a sensation; asserting that an object 'has a virtue' is merely restating the observed fact.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not explain observable regularities by inventing unobservable powers when the regularity (object → sensation) suffices; the opium-soporific example illustrates this anti‑occult-cause caution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation grounded in a shared fact (fundamentum relationis)
rubrics_metrics.description: A relation between two things is grounded on some fact or phenomenon in which the two things jointly enter—the Aristotelian 'fundamentum relationis' (e.g., master/servant grounded on services performed; greater/less grounded on inclusion of space).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For logical analysis identify the fact or series of facts (resolvable into states of consciousness) that constitutes the fundamentum of any relation named; relations supervene on such shared phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likeness/unlikeness and succession/simultaneity are sui generis (states of consciousness)
rubrics_metrics.description: The simple relations of likeness/unlikeness and of antecedence/simultaneity are peculiar: they are themselves states of consciousness (feelings of resemblance, of succession) and do not admit the same kind of analysis as other relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize these relations as primitive in analysis; while complex likenesses can be resolved into part-likenesses, the feeling of resemblance or succession is presupposed in any further analysis and may be unanalyzable within logic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantity grounded in difference of sensations
rubrics_metrics.description: Differences of quantity (e.g., a gallon vs ten gallons) are grounded on differences in the sensations produced by those quantities; quantity is the aspect in which sensations resemble or differ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When asserting quantitative difference, treat it as a claim about differing sensory or experiential profiles rather than about an independently known 'bulk' beyond sensations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributes of minds: internal states and effects on other minds
rubrics_metrics.description: Attributes ascribed to minds may refer either to the mind's own habitual states (e.g., meditative, cheerful) or to the feelings which contemplation of that mind excites in others (e.g., admiration); many predications of character are twofold.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When predicating qualities of persons, distinguish between (1) the internal series of feelings that characterize the mind and (2) the responses those states produce in other minds (approval, approbation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxonomy of Feelings for logical analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Feelings are of four sorts: Sensations, Thoughts, Emotions, and Volitions; Perceptions are a particular case of Belief; Actions are volitions followed by an effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this classification as the basis for resolving substances and attributes into elements of consciousness when performing logical analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: For logical proof, sensations are the only essential/provable part of attributes
rubrics_metrics.description: In predicating qualities, the only part which logic can and needs to prove is the sensation (the foundation); the rest (an alleged inherent 'power') is unnecessary for logical demonstration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analytical and evidential claims in logic should focus on establishing the relevant sensations/states of consciousness rather than hypothesizing unobservable properties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish identity from undistinguishable resemblance in language
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an ambiguity in using the word 'same' to denote identity vs perfect resemblance (e.g., 'the same sensation' today and yesterday). Mistaking resemblance for identity produces fallacies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful in predication and argument to distinguish true identity (one and the same entity) from mere undistinguishableness or exact resemblance of separate occurrences or objects.
